$note: A REWRITE STATION: the same shape as Reading/Database/templates/by_axis/json, sparse (only the fields this model wrote), never the truth. Adopt a field into the final template station with adopt.mjs on the owner's ruling.

angles.drive: Learning a thing your own way matters more to you than the approved way. Since you need to understand before you trust, you take the side door into a subject rather than the front one. Let someone walk that route with you sometimes, because a way only you know is lonely to own.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you want to know something, you find it out yourself instead of asking someone who knows. Owning an answer is worth a month to you where borrowing takes an hour, so the month comes out of your rest. Ask for the hour now and again, because being taught makes the knowing no less yours.
angles.cost_others: The lesson you teach yourself is the one you rarely pass on. You learn by a route too odd to explain, so you keep the knowing rather than the telling. Hand one person the messy version, because what you keep unexplained is what the people learning from you go without.

angles.drive: The hunch reaches you before the reason does, and you take it seriously. Because you need to know a thing from underneath rather than from its surface, you read what lies under what is said. You cannot always explain it, so let the reason catch up before you act on it.
angles.cost_self: Where you are quickest is where you are hardest to follow, so you know before you can explain. You act on the read rather than wait for proof, which puts the doubt on you until proof arrives. Write the hunch down and give it a day, because being right in silence wears you down.
angles.cost_others: Reading what people leave unsaid is how you understand them, and how you skip asking. Since the read arrives before the question would, you answer what sits under the words rather than the words themselves. Ask the plain question every so often, because you cost the people you read the chance to say it themselves.

angles.drive: You do your best thinking with no one else in the house. Being alone is where the taking in happens for you, so you want the quiet ahead of the company. You pay for it in company that thins out on its own, which is why one open evening a week is worth keeping.
angles.cost_self: Whenever a day has held too many people, you need an hour with none to feel yourself. Time alone is how you fill back up rather than hide, which is why you guard it harder than your sleep. Guard the sleep too, since the quiet you take from the night was owed to the body.
angles.cost_others: Your quiet is a place you go without saying how long you will be. Because you think best out of reach, you let the hours alone run past what you promised rather than stop early. Name the length before you go, since you owe the people waiting a time to expect you.

angles.drive: One more source always feels wiser than a first try. You have more Earth than your core gets through, so you keep taking in rather than putting out, since intake feels like progress. Keep in mind that you will not read your way to ready, because starting is the only thing that gets you there.
angles.cost_self: Reading up on a thing is where you feel most in control. Since the next page asks nothing of you while the first try asks everything, you stay in the pages past the point of use. Remember, you pay in real time, and your body keeps the count even when you lose it.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you owe someone an answer, you give them your preparation instead of the answer. Being ready counts for more with you than being on time, which puts the people who asked on your clock. Remember that you were asked for the rough thing you have, and you keep them waiting on polish.

angles.drive: Going quiet is where you go before anything has gone wrong. Solitude is how you take things in, and you take in rather than reach out, so you let the gap between replies grow. Remember that you can keep the quiet and close the gap in the same week.
angles.cost_self: The quiet you keep protects you from less than it costs you. Because being reached feels like being spent, you let the phone go dark ahead of answering, until alone stops being a choice. Remember that the peace costs you loneliness afterward, and you pay less when you take less at once.
angles.cost_others: Going into your own head takes you out of reach of people counting on you. Thinking alone works better for you than talking, so you let a week pass rather than send a line and call it concentration. Try to remember that you leave them guessing, and one short reply costs less than the guessing.

angles.drive: Whenever a decision is nearly made, you find one more angle to see it from. You hold more Earth than you spend, so you turn a thing over again rather than settle it. Remember that you usually land on your first read anyway, and you pay for the weeks between with sleep.
angles.cost_self: The second thought is where most of your time goes. Since you need to feel sure before moving, you keep turning a choice over rather than act on it, long after it stops helping. Remember that waiting to feel sure differs from working to be sure, and you trade rest for the wait.
angles.cost_others: Thinking it over once more is how you keep people waiting on an answer you have. Being certain comes first for you, so you hold the yes or no for weeks rather than give a maybe. Remember that you take from them the plain answer, and an early maybe costs you less than silence.

angles.drive: Taking things in whole is how your mind works, even when the world calls it slowness. You do not sample, you absorb, and what you absorb becomes permanent equipment. Understanding, for you, is not a pass through the material. It is ownership.
angles.cost_self: One book, read twice, with notes in the margins the second time through. That is your whole method, and it quietly beats the forty skimmed summaries everyone else is stacking. Ask you about it in a year and it is still there, organized and ready.
angles.cost_others: People mistake your pace for being behind, right up until they need someone who actually understood the material. Then they come to you. What reads as slow from the outside is your mind refusing to accept anything it has not fully chewed.

angles.drive: Waiting before you speak is a habit you built on purpose, and it earns its keep. Your thinking has one speed, thorough, and pressure has never successfully changed the setting. What comes out late comes out finished, and people have learned the trade is worth it.
angles.cost_self: The meeting moves fast, everyone answers inside five seconds, and you say nothing for a while. Then your answer arrives, last and unhurried, and it is the one that ends up in the notes. It took you longer because you were finishing the thought.
angles.cost_others: Faster colleagues sometimes read your silence as having nothing to say. The ones who stay long enough learn the pattern: pressure speeds everyone else up and leaves your pace exactly where it was. What you lose in quickness you keep collecting back in accuracy.

angles.drive: Your best ideas come in from odd corners, and trusting them is a skill worth building. Your mind connects things underground, without appointments, and hands the results up when they are ready. The sources look random to everyone else. The record says otherwise.
angles.cost_self: The answer to a work problem shows up while you are reading a cookbook, or on a bus, or inside an uncle’s offhand story. It happens too often to be luck. Your mind connects things underground, in the dark, and hands you the result later like it was easy.
angles.cost_others: Nobody watching you would call it research. A cookbook here, a detour there, an afternoon lost to something unrelated, and then you surface with an idea no straight line could have reached. The people who work in straight lines have learned to stop asking how.

angles.drive: Pulling back is where you rest, long before it is any kind of reaction. Company drains a battery in you that solitude recharges, and the door drifts toward closed on its own schedule. Nothing has to go wrong first. The pulling back is the baseline.
angles.cost_self: Three drafts of a two-line reply sit on your phone, and the phone sits face-down through dinner. Nothing about the message is hard. The withdrawing happens earlier than that, somewhere between thinking a thing and letting anyone watch you think it.
angles.cost_others: People stop hearing from you and assume something happened. Usually nothing did, and that is the part worth noticing: the quiet was never a response to anything. Given no reason at all, your door still drifts toward closed, and someone else always has to knock first.

angles.drive: Holding a thought long after it stops being useful is your mind’s oldest habit. What enters you does not leave on time: it settles, replays, and files itself under unfinished, permanently. All that replaying feels like processing. Mostly it is wear.
angles.cost_self: It is Thursday night and Tuesday’s conversation is still running, paused at the one sentence you would take back. You have replayed it enough times to know it will not change, and you replay it anyway, because putting a thought down was never something anyone taught you.
angles.cost_others: From the outside you just seem quiet. Inside, a committee has been in session since Tuesday, reviewing one sentence from a conversation everyone else forgot. What people read as calm is often storage, thoughts settling in layers and staying down longer than they ever needed to.

angles.drive: Getting ready is where you hide, and it photographs as diligence from every angle. As long as you are still preparing, nobody can grade the real attempt, and part of you has arranged your studying life around that protection. Somewhere the preparing stopped serving the step and started replacing it.
angles.cost_self: Seventeen browser tabs, two saved courses, a notebook full of plans. The project they all point at has not moved in a month, but the researching of it has never gone better. One more book, you tell yourself, and the telling sounds exactly like last time.
angles.cost_others: To everyone watching, you are the responsible one, always studying, always ready. Only you know the math underneath: as long as you are still getting ready, nobody can say you failed. It is a clever shelter, and it keeps out progress as reliably as it keeps out judgment.
